name: Monoceros
introduction: is the Unicorn, a faint constellation introduced in the early 17th century, lying within the Winter Triangle of Betelgeuse, Procyon and Sirius. Although its stars are dim, the Milky Way passes through it, making it rich in clusters and nebulae.

sections.title: What makes it special
paragraphs: Monoceros is a nursery of stars. The Rosette Nebula surrounds a young cluster whose radiation has hollowed out its center, and the Christmas Tree Cluster lies near the dark Cone Nebula.
In 2002, the star V838 Monocerotis suddenly flared, and its light echoed through the surrounding dust, illuminating shells of material.

sections.title: Notable stars
paragraphs: [Beta Monocerotis](hip:30867) is one of the finest triple stars in a small telescope; William Herschel called it one of the most beautiful sights in the heavens. [Alpha Monocerotis](hip:37447) is an orange giant.
[Scholz’s Star](id:cns5-1819), a faint red dwarf with a brown dwarf companion, passed through the outer Oort Cloud of our Solar System about 70,000 years ago, the closest known flyby of another star.

sections.title: Beyond the stars
paragraphs: Monoceros also contains Hubble’s Variable Nebula, a fan of light that changes shape from month to month, and Plaskett’s Star, one of the most massive binary stars known.
